newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Front month gas oil eases.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Front month gas oil eases.

text.p: Singapore gas oil front month swaps eased slightly at midday on Monday but was steady further out on expectations of regional demand in lacklustre trading, brokers said.
"The market is very quiet this morning and no trades were seen," one broker said, alluding to the typical quiet Monday morning trading.

The front month January eased by about 20 cents to $31.80/$32.10 per barrel from Friday's quotes. Traders said this was due to market perceptions that most consumers have covered their January requirement.
"The focus has moved to February," one trader said.
February gas oil opened unchanged from Friday at $31.05/$31.20 per barrel, brokers said.
As a result the January/February time spread crunched slightly to $0.75/$0.95 per barrel from Friday's $0.85/$1.00.
Traders said February swaps was steady despite Friday's lower January gas oil close on the International Petroleum Exchange which ended down a $4.50 per tonne higher at $227.50 per tonne.
February held its own due to expectations of further buying from regional consumers such as China, Indonesia and India, traders said.
Fuel oil and naphtha were largely unchanged from Friday in quiet trading with January fuel oil quoted notionally at $120.50/$122.00 per tonne and naphtha at $24.80/$25.00 per barrel.
